name: Chennai
tagline: World-Class Healthcare and Coastal Calm on the Bay of Bengal
description: Chennai is South India's cultural and economic anchor, a Bay of Bengal capital where Tamil temple traditions, a thriving auto and IT industry, and some of the country's best hospitals all converge. Known as the 'Health Capital of India,' the city is home to Apollo Hospitals and a dense cluster of internationally accredited medical centers, making it a natural fit for retirees who prioritize healthcare access. Coastal neighborhoods along the Marina and East Coast Road offer a calmer, more laid-back pace than Delhi or Mumbai, with a strong Tamil cultural identity running through daily life. Heat and humidity are constant companions, but the combination of medical infrastructure and low costs is difficult to match elsewhere in Asia.

quickFacts.visa: India has no retirement, pension, or passive-income visa. US citizens use the e-Tourist visa — 30-day (double-entry) or 1-year/5-year (multiple-entry; the 5-year fee rose from $80 to $200 in 2026) — and may stay up to 180 days per visit, with total time capped at 180 days per calendar year; long-term residents get by cycling visas in and out. The only path to living in India indefinitely is the OCI card, open to people of Indian origin or those married 2+ years to an Indian citizen or OCI holder.
quickFacts.internetSpeed: 60–100 Mbps typical; fiber widely available to 1 Gbps
quickFacts.safetyRating: One of India's safer big cities, often rated good for women; heat, monsoon flooding, and traffic are the practical concerns
quickFacts.climate: Tropical and coastal — hot and humid most of the year with an October–December northeast monsoon

healthcare.description: Private health insurance with access to Apollo and MIOT International hospital networks

1M.lifestyle: A comfortable 2-bedroom apartment in Anna Nagar or Adyar, getting around on the growing Chennai Metro plus autos and ride-hailing apps. Eating at Tamil thali counters and casual dosa restaurants most days, with occasional nicer meals out. Private health insurance covers Apollo and MIOT International, giving easy access to some of India's best hospitals. Heat and humidity are constant, but day-to-day costs are very low and healthcare peace of mind comes standard.
